runs.content: Monday's rotation focus is Finance + Crypto. Since the last thinker run (2026-09-13, Sunday), log.md shows only two mechanical Finance tracker refreshes (sector-performance-tracker, growth-value-tracker) plus a Strategy Feedback review and the routine end-of-day memory update — no new source material was clipped or ingested, an unusually quiet window. Deep-read Finance's newest model page, finance/models/model-hyperscaler-debt-capex-rate-exposure-2026-09-10.md (built 2026-09-10, SEC EDGAR debt/capex/rate-exposure ranking across MSFT/AMZN/GOOGL/META/ORCL/CRWV/PLTR), and Crypto's core pages (crypto-overview, crypto-portfolio, defi-watchlist) in full. One genuinely new, non-duplicate investigation idea cleared the bar: the model page's own Data Source Note describes the tool that produced it — `carry-trade-debt-monitor`, a self-hosted SEC EDGAR XBRL scraper with a live dashboard (localhost:8420) that has now underpinned two separate Finance models — as 'not yet published to the wiki as its own project.' A grep of wiki/ai-tech/ confirms it: ai-tech/projects.md, the domain's own 'All software/app/AI projects' index, still lists exactly one entry (Crypto App) plus an empty placeholder row, unchanged since 2026-05-01. This is the identical pattern the wiki-thinker already caught and closed for Lightfin's AI-video pipeline on 2026-07-17 — a real, actively-used AI build invisible from the one page meant to catalog it — just recurring for a different tool. Crypto's own pages (overview, portfolio, defi-watchlist) were read in full but turned up nothing new: the one live cross-domain thread there (SmarDex's USDN stablecoin vs. the Bessent Treasury-reserve stablecoin thesis) is already cross-linked in defi-watchlist.md's own See Also. No new cross-domain connection cleared the bar today. Checked the open sections for resolution: nothing showed clear signs of being actioned since 2026-09-13.

Sunday's rotation focus is 'whichever domain has gone longest without a deep-dive.' Among the Friday-group domains (Lightfin, Games, Cooking, Sports Betting, Work), Lightfin was covered last Sunday (2026-09-06), so today's deep-read targeted Games — unchanged since the 2026-07-27 discovery that all four prototype stubs are real files, just filed under the wrong domain folders; games/overview.md and games/prototypes.md are still the exact same unpopulated placeholder tables from 2026-05-01, and raw/games/ has no new files. Nothing new surfaced there. Since the last thinker run (2026-09-12, Saturday full sweep), log.md otherwise shows only routine Finance-internal activity: an mf-update Magic Formula run and the first-ever run of the new strategy-feedback-loop task (added 2026-09-10) confirming its own Burry-aware entry-avoidance rule worked as designed (MU/QCOM/ASML/CAT drove the worst paper-trading losses in strategies B/C/D) — already correctly wired into finance/models/model-portfolio-management.md, not a gap. Two genuinely new, non-duplicate cross-domain connections cleared the bar instead, both from Saturday's podcast-summarizer batch that hadn't yet been checked against Finance: (1) Ed Zitron's newly-ingested 'AI is the world's greatest bubble' episode (podcast-diary-of-a-ceo-ed-zitron-episode, circular financing between hyperscalers and AI labs, dot-com parallels) makes almost the identical argument finance/models/model-hyperscaler-gpu-token-debt-2026-08-05.md already built a full off-balance-sheet debt map around — that model page explicitly cross-references Burry's own circular-financing thesis and the BIS Annual Economic Report, but nothing links it to Zitron's episode, which currently only cross-links within Podcasts. (2) Dividend Talk EP 305 ('Should Cyclical Stocks Be in Your Dividend Portfolio') names exactly the dividend-safety test missing from finance/ideas/ideas-dividend-undervalued.md, which already carries two cyclical names (AGCO, Lithia Motors) flagged internally as riskier picks but never tested against a cyclical-vs-compounder framework — its own 'What Makes a Dividend Sustainable' section only covers moat, capital allocation, and undervaluation. Checked the open sections for resolution: nothing showed clear signs of being actioned since 2026-09-12.
